precepts.text: Though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more. And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it. That word that you hear is how you are born of the spirit.
precepts.point: The wind bloweth where it listeth: that wind blowing where it will is the word of God. You do not know who the word of God is going to affect. Thou hearest the sound thereof: we heard this truth, we heard that call, and it activated us. The Lord has his agents on the earth; you hear a certain word and you wake up. So is every one that is born of the Spirit.

note.label: Born for Adversity

precepts.why:
“Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” Christ says “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” What is that really saying? Isaiah shows it.

“And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.” That word you hear, this is the way, walk ye in it, is how you are born. That is how you are born of the spirit.

The wind that blows where it will is the word of God. You don't know who the word of God is going to affect. The sound thereof is “This is the way, walk ye in it”, the word of God. Every last one of us in here heard the truth, heard that sound, heard that call, and it activated us. The Lord has his agents on the earth, like sleeper cells: you just hear a certain trigger word behind you and you activate, you wake up to this truth. The Bible is the activation.

And notice what comes with it: the bread of adversity and the water of affliction. A brother is born for adversity. When you are born into this truth and depart from evil, you make yourself a prey; Satan comes for you, and you will have to go through things. But the teachers are no longer hid in a corner, and the word behind you keeps you walking in the way.

precepts.text: He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already. And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. They hate Christ and the commandments because coming to the light reproves the deeds. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God. We want the word of God to make our deeds manifest: Lord, show me what I am.
precepts.point: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. And he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: when you repent and come to this truth, everybody around you starts hating you. And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

precepts.text: Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
precepts.point: The Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt be turned into another man. You don't believe that you could become a whole different person; the scripture says you can.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

precepts.why:
A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.

precepts.text: After the civil rights era Christianity changed from the Klan's white Jesus to God loves everybody and all-inclusive churches; the lamb's horns and the dragon's voice, a doctrine of adaptation, while the truth cannot adapt.
precepts.point: The 1960s and the 1990s were the two waves: the truth began in 1969 and the one-West teachers came in the 1990s, so Esau hit each wave with the Bible revisions, the vaccine schedule, crack, the three-strikes law and the prison pipeline.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
The plan said the old religions will have to go, and that goes into Christianity itself changing. Before the civil rights movement, Christianity was used to oppress us. A lot of the KKK were Christians. The white man would tell you straight that he was worshipping white Jesus and lynching you, and that you could not pray for him; you couldn't go to a white church. White people were just conquering and destroying everybody.

After the civil rights era they started changing Christianity up. Now they started implementing John 3:16, and Galatians, and saying everybody can go to heaven and God loves everybody. Christianity became all-inclusive, and it was not like that sixty years ago.

That goes back to Revelation, the beast with two horns like a lamb that spake as a dragon. The same people who taught the old white Christianity changed the face of it, but the voice is still the dragon's. It is the same trick as civil rights: the ostensible purpose is that black people get their rights, and the real purpose is rights for every heathen to exploit us, while black schools and black businesses that were thriving fail.

Christianity is a doctrine of adaptation, and so the white man's religion adapted when it needed to. The truth cannot adapt. That is how Daniel 7:25 is fulfilled: he thinks to change times and laws, and even the teaching of his religion is changed to keep our people from the laws and commandments of God.

precepts.text: This is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
precepts.point: Seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel stood with censers in the dark, saying, the Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth. What do you do in the dark? Your secret sins.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

precepts.why:
Ezekiel was shown “what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in the chambers of his imagery? for they say, The Lord seeth us not; the Lord hath forsaken the earth.” Seventy elders with censers in their hands, burning incense to the images in the dark. What do they do in the dark? What do you do in the dark? Your secrets, your secret sins.

Christ gives the judgment on it: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men love the dark because their deeds are evil; they hide there because they think the Lord does not see them.

But the Lord brought Ezekiel through the hole in the wall to show him exactly what was done in the dark. Nothing done in the chambers of imagery is hidden from him. The ancients said the Lord had forsaken the earth, but it was they who had forsaken the light, and that is the condemnation.

precepts.text: Men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. There are people who were ordained of old to stay like that; God gave them up to strong delusion, and some people are bound in that darkness.
precepts.point: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh: other nations, and worse, as it is today. They are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire: that lake of fire we read about in Revelation 14.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Jude says the angels which kept not their first estate are reserved “in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.” Has that great day come yet, brothers? No. Those sons of God who went in unto the daughters of men were destroyed in the flood, and those spirits came right back, by way of the three sons, Ham, Shem and Japheth. They are still here today.

John shows what that darkness is: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Men loving darkness rather than light is sin: you hate God's laws, you hate this truth, you hate the Bible.

There are people like that who were ordained of old to stay like that, the “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation”. Remember 2 Thessalonians: God gave them up to strong delusion, that they should believe a lie and not repent and come into the light. Some people are bound in that darkness, and there is nothing you can do for them. That is the chains of darkness, reserved unto the judgment of the great day.

precepts.text: Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people, which in time past were not a people but are now the people of God. In the days of Peter the northern kingdom was not counted a people; after emancipation we were counted three-fifths of a man and still called property, walking about with signs reading I am a man. We had not obtained mercy in slavery; now the truth is coming out that we are the people of God.
precepts.point: Those verses only began to be preached about black and brown people once the civil rights movement started, and that is why the churches will not look at these images; the pictures contradict what they say John 3:16 and Galatians 3:28 mean.

note.label: The Fallacy of Black Christians

precepts.point: Those verses only began to be preached about black and brown people once the civil rights movement started, and that is why the churches will not look at these images; the pictures contradict what they say John 3:16 and Galatians 3:28 mean.

precepts.point: Those verses only began to be preached about black and brown people once the civil rights movement started, and that is why the churches will not look at these images; the pictures contradict what they say John 3:16 and Galatians 3:28 mean.

precepts.text: Nicodemus, a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, came to Christ by night; an Israelite came to an Israelite.
precepts.point: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

note.label: Numbers 21: The Fiery Serpents and the Serpent of Brass

precepts.why:
Christ brought the serpent of brass to Nicodemus. “There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: The same came to Jesus by night, and said unto him, Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.”

Nicodemus was a Pharisee, a ruler of the Jews, and he came to Christ, who is also a Jew: an Israelite came to an Israelite. Two Israelites speaking together about the history of Israel, the fiery serpents that bit the people and the serpent of brass on the pole.

precepts.text: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish.
precepts.point: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. And the whosoever is defined in Acts: whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved; ye men of Israel, hear these words. The salvation spoken of is for Israel.

note.label: Numbers 21: The Fiery Serpents and the Serpent of Brass

precepts.why:
Moses “made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.” Read it with the nation in view: the people being bitten, the people dying, all of it is Israel. That brass serpent was for the Israelites, to heal the Israelites, because it was the Israelites being bitten for rebelling against God and against Moses. The symbol on ambulances today, a snake wrapped around a pole, comes from this scripture.

Christ told Nicodemus, “And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.”

As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness to save Israel from death, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: the same way Israel beheld the serpent and did not perish, whosoever believes on Christ shall not perish but have eternal life. The serpent healed Israel; the Son of man lifted up saves Israel.

precepts.text: This is one of those lies learned under the false image, telling everybody on the earth that God so loved the whole world.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” This is one of those lies learned under the false image, the teacher of lies: telling everybody on the earth that God so loved the whole world.

That is what the graven image teaches. The psalm says our God is in the heavens and his glory is not unto us but unto his name, for his mercy and for his truth's sake, and they that trust in the image are like unto it.

precepts.text: The wind bloweth where it listeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit. The word rests on those it is given to.
precepts.point: Whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance; but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.

note.label: Matthew 13: The Parables of the Kingdom

precepts.why:
“Why speakest thou unto them in parables?” “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” The mysteries are given to some and not to others. “For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath.”

Christ told Nicodemus how that works: “The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” The wind goes where it will, and you cannot say where it comes from or where it goes; so is every one born of the Spirit. The word rests on those it is given to. That is why it is given to the disciples to know the mysteries and not to the others, and why the one who has receives more while the one who has not loses even what he has.

precepts.text: He gave his only begotten Son. A father and a son are two, which is what the verse says on its face.
precepts.point: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” The Word was made flesh, and we beheld his glory, “the glory as of the only begotten of the Father”; here Christ says whose only begotten Son that is. God gave his Son.

A father and a son are two, which is what the verse says on its face. The Father gave; the Son was given. The Word made flesh that dwelt among us, full of grace and truth, is the only begotten Son of the Father, not the Father himself.

precepts.text: If so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive, and after death ye shall obtain mercy.
precepts.point: This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night. Those men were the teachers of the synagogues, and it would have cost him standing to come openly. And Christ told him, “Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

This is spoken to a man who believed himself already right. Ezra gives the same thing: “Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.” To be born again, a man has to subdue his own understanding and reform his heart.

Sinners and publicans received Christ more readily because they knew they needed a saviour; a ruler of the Jews had to start over. Subdue your own understanding, and you shall be kept alive, and after death obtain mercy.

precepts.text: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.
precepts.point: Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. Both are named plainly elsewhere as the word.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Nicodemus took it literally and asked whether a man can “enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born”. Christ answered, “Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.”

Peter tells what that birth is: “Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.” Being born again is by the word of God. Both the water and the Spirit are named plainly elsewhere as the word. It is not a second birth from a mother's womb; it is a birth of incorruptible seed, the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever.

precepts.text: So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.
precepts.point: A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.” Paul draws the line: “So then they that are in the flesh cannot please God.”

A man left in the flesh will do the works of the flesh, and those works are named in the epistles. That which is born of the flesh stays flesh, and they that are in the flesh cannot please God. That is why Christ says, “Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.” A man must be born of the Spirit to please God.

precepts.text: Much people of Israel died, and every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
precepts.point: The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up”. The history behind that is plain, and so is who it was for. “And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.”

“And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.” It was Israel in the wilderness that spake against the Most High and against Moses, and Israel that was bitten. “Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord, and against thee; pray unto the Lord, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.”

“And the Lord said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.” It was Israel that looked and lived. Even so the Son of man was lifted up, “That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life”: the same people, bitten, looking, and living.

precepts.text: They were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.
precepts.point: The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
Solomon tells what the serpent of brass was: “For when the horrible fierceness of beasts came upon these, and they perished with the stings of crooked serpents, thy wrath endured not for ever: But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of thy law.”

The serpent of brass was a sign of salvation, and it came with remembrance of the commandment of the law. They were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished. Looking on it was not the whole of it; there was repentance with it. They had said, “We have sinned, for we have spoken against the Lord”, and the sign put them in remembrance of the commandment of the law.

So when the Son of man is lifted up like that serpent, believing in him goes with the same thing: remembrance of the commandment of the law, and repentance.

precepts.text: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; that he should be made manifest to Israel.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son”. This follows straight on from the serpent lifted up in the wilderness for Israel, and it is the same people in view. John's own gospel names who the world is.

John the Baptist said, “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” Then he said why he came: “And I knew him not: but that he should be made manifest to Israel, therefore am I come baptizing with water.” The Lamb that takes away the sin of the world was to be made manifest to Israel. The world whose sin he takes away is the one he was made manifest to: Israel.

precepts.text: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“On the next day much people that were come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, Took branches of palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried, Hosanna: Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.”

Much people came to the feast and cried out that he is the King of Israel. That multitude was Israel, and it is that same multitude the Pharisees are speaking of next when they say the world is gone after him. So the world in “God so loved the world” is that people, the ones who called him the King of Israel.

precepts.text: The Pharisees said, Behold, the world is gone after him, of that same multitude.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him.”

The Pharisees said the world is gone after him, of that same multitude that took branches of palm trees and cried, “Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord.” That multitude was the world. John's own gospel uses the word that way, so “God so loved the world” is speaking of that people, the same ones the serpent was lifted up for.

precepts.text: I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.”

He spake openly to the world, and then he says where: in the synagogue and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort. The world he taught openly was the Jews in the synagogue and the temple. Put it with the one he was made manifest to and the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the world God so loved is named plainly in John's own gospel.

precepts.text: He that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.
precepts.point: He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true.” John writes the other side of that in his epistle: “He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.”

Not to receive his testimony is to call the record God gave of his son a lie. He that believes on the Son has the witness in himself, and has set to his seal that God is true; he that believes not has made God a liar. That is why “he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.”

precepts.text: The verse used for a universal whosoever, but in Acts 2 the whosoever is answered by "ye men of Israel."
precepts.point: "Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved" is defined by its audience. It is not the universal whosoever the churches pull from John 3:16; the whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
This is the verse the churches pull a universal whosoever from: “that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” But a whosoever is defined by who is being spoken to.

In Acts 2 Peter says whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved, and the very next verse answers who that is: ye men of Israel. Joel said the same, that the Most High is in the midst of Israel and deliverance is in Zion and Jerusalem. The whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands, not all nations.

precepts.text: John said, He must increase, but I must decrease; he understood his mission and did not get bent out of shape, the same way a father in the faith teaches all he knows and then brings the student to one who knows more.
precepts.point: This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“He must increase, but I must decrease.” John understood his mission and his place, and did not get bent out of shape when his disciples went to Christ. It is the same way a father in the faith teaches all he knows and then brings the student to one who knows more.

That is how Philip comes to baptize the eunuch in water. Some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism, even though Christ's baptism is not water. John pointed them to Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. Sin's pleasure is temporary. A brother or sister arranges a meeting through Facebook, enjoys fifteen or thirty minutes, then finds out they contracted a disease. Was that pleasure worth it? They ask why God did it while forgetting their own choice.

The drug dealer makes quick money but is always looking over his shoulder, worried about the police or another dealer who wants to take him out. That is no way to live. The pleasure lasts only a season and brings consequences; choose affliction with God's people over that darkness.
